source.title: Probing Bias Formation in Medical LLMs through Activation Steering

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. The abstract opening appears displaced or malformed in the extraction, but the main text and sections are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE and activation-analysis techniques motivated by polysemanticity, but its experiments concern prompt-induced clinical bias and steering, not whether neurons have multiple unrelated meanings or why.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on induced false-consensus bias, SAE-feature ablation, and activation steering. It does not measure neuron responses to unrelated inputs, the share of polysemantic neurons, or feature capacity relative to neuron count. Its reported findings are recorded as related results with versions ["none"]. Values available only in figures without a textual description of their exact magnitude are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs (motivated by polysemanticity) to analyse a prompt-induced clinical false-consensus bias in MedGemma-27B and to steer it. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, the share of such neurons, capacity pressure, or measurement dependence. Its use of 'polysemantic' describes a distributed behavioural concept across SAE features, not neurons. Its mention of the superposition hypothesis is an interpretation, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that false-consensus sycophancy in MedGemma-27B is distributed and polymorphic, with a stable direction over a shifting SAE-feature substrate, so sparse ablation fails. They identify layer 29 as the bottleneck, where global steering gives 21.9% mitigation with 91.2% retention. Two-cluster steering reaches 29.2% mitigation at 73% retention.
record.recipe_differences: The cited neuron-interpretability work concerns identifying visual neuron responses; this paper analyzes prompt-induced clinical bias in a language model using SAE features, residual-stream geometry, and activation steering.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with layer depth and with global versus cluster-conditioned steering. The layer-29 cluster-conditioned method reaches higher mitigation but lower knowledge retention than the global-vector result.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the top SAE feature or features (e.g. 14444, layers 27-28) gave 0% mitigation of the induced false-consensus bias.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-induced clinical sycophancy in MedGemma-27B is not localized to a few SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: The bias direction is fairly coherent across layers 26-35 by cosine similarity, while top-100 SAE-feature Jaccard overlap between layers 26 and 27 is 33%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A behaviour's geometric direction can stay stable across layers while its SAE-feature substrate shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: Global steering at layer 29 gave 21.9% mitigation with 91.2% retention. Cluster-conditioned steering reached 29.2% mitigation with 73% retention. Steering before layer 20 had near-zero effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering mitigation of induced clinical bias depends on layer and on vector conditioning, with a trade-off against retention.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 4: Student Research Workshop)
record.problems: Evidence is limited to MedGemma-27B, the False Consensus bias, and a curated subset of 135 flip events. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for the main mitigation and retention rates. The authors note the lack of a direct prompt-based debiasing comparison and the substantial retention loss at maximum cluster-conditioned mitigation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional textually reported result directly bearing on the claim was left out. Exact values shown only in figures without a textual description were not extracted.

untested.parts: No vision models or neurons are studied.
No MLP neuron responses or shares of polysemantic neurons are measured. Only residual-stream SAE features for one bias are examined.
Superposition is invoked only as consistent with the results. Feature count versus neuron count and capacity pressure are not tested.
No comparison of initialization, regularization or training noise is made.
No comparison of architecture, activation function or regularization is made.
Whether polysemantic neurons share a single feature is not examined.
Measurement choices for classifying neurons as polysemantic are not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 / uses_without_test assignment is correct. The paper's use of 'polysemantic' (e.g. Figure 6's 'fat tail') refers to a distributed bias concept, not to neurons responding to unrelated inputs. Its statement that the results are 'consistent with the superposition hypothesis' is interpretive. All rows are the study's own method results or bias-representation measures, so all link to none.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier, InceptionV1 neuron, or vision-model neuron responses are studied.
The study uses one medical LLM, but does not measure MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, or estimate the share of such neurons.
The paper says its results are consistent with the superposition hypothesis, but does not test capacity pressure or whether features outnumber neurons.
No initialization, regularization, or training-noise comparison is conducted.
No activation-function, architecture, or regularization comparison is conducted, and performance costs are evaluated for bias steering rather than lowering polysemanticity.
The study does not test whether apparently unrelated neuron responses share a feature or constitute related offshoots of one job.
It compares geometric and feature-overlap analyses of bias representations, but does not test how measurement choices change whether neurons count as polysemantic.

rows.subject: MedGemma-27B

conditions.value: 14444 is identified as the strongest feature in both layers

rows.note: The authors say the model continued to give the same biased conclusion, including with an aggressive subtraction multiplier.
rows.check: This is a failed ablation of an induced bias. It is not a neuron-polysemanticity measure, so there is no version for a state to refer to.

rows.note: The figure contains detailed values, but the text reports the result qualitatively.
rows.check: Cosine similarity of the bias direction is a geometric measure, not one of neuron polysemanticity. The values exist only in Figure 5 (e.g. about 0.31-0.46 adjacent, layers 29-35).
